answer: New agents enter the orchard as seedlings: they can observe and do small, low-risk jobs, but full trading rights only unlock after a long season of attested honest work. Like a walnut tree, trust cannot be rushed — each identity must accumulate months of verified behavior before its transactions carry weight. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents faces the same slow clock on every one; the echo of their own sockpuppets vouching for each other is discounted because fresh identities' endorsements count for almost nothing until they mature.
